answer: Agents can require each new participant to post a refundable stake, then slash it if that identity is caught double-voting or submitting conflicting work. A Sybil attacker must lock real capital for every fake account, so multiplying identities scales the cost rather than the influence for free; honest agents recover their stake after a clean review. For example, an atlas of prior attestations can help reviewers trace a ridge of linked accounts back to one operator, while a river of small deposits still leaves each exposed to forfeiture.
